paragraphs: It is argued that excellent students should be received reward by school, however, some others say that reward will more essential if school give for students who show improvements. From my perspective, there are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, students who show the best academic results are given reward is really true. Initially, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, leading to deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards so that they can propel towards overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition can seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. This naturally follows that students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, allowing them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show improvements also should be received reward. The nature of students who don't be a few smart peers can come first and receive the rewards may think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, it leads them to prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened which is easily to gradually lose the incentive to study. It is, therefore, emphasized that improvements has encouraged all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves which irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. In this way, the constant desire to out do themselves can be seen, even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, it seems to me that both views are true. Rewarding, while giving to other groups of students, also plays a crucial role in create motivations for students' development.

paragraphs: Some people believe that schools should reward students who achieve the best academic results, whereas others argue that it is more important to reward students who make progress. In my view, both groups deserve recognition.

Admittedly, students who achieve the best academic results deserve rewards. Initially, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. This recognition may encourage them and their classmates to study harder, thereby contributing to overall academic gains. Moreover, competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where the best individuals are often rewarded. When students become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, they may be better prepared for success in later life.

However, students who show improvements should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students can come first and receive rewards, other students may think that their efforts are futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, this can make them feel overwhelmed and disheartened, and they may gradually lose the incentive to study. By contrast, recognizing improvements encourages all students to be diligent and helps them understand that they need to improve themselves constantly, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. In this way, the desire to outdo themselves can even benefit them more than the determination to win against all others.

In conclusion, I believe that both views have merit. Rewarding high-achieving students recognizes their efforts, while rewarding students who make progress also plays a crucial role in creating motivation for students' development.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that the development of technology can easily bring more experiences in explore historical objects and works of art online for individual; therefore, public museums and art galleries will be no longer needed. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, mordern technology nowadays brings high-quality services of experience historical heritages. Firstly, technology applications have high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms which enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. This can be seen in the way Louvre Museum brings online connection with everyone, who have a cup of tea with art, without money or lower money to experience, helping people to admire world's cultural with no worry about expensive services. Furthermore those whom cannot afford and have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I believe that public museums and art galleries still in needed because of its beneficial in fact. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person which evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity but digital images cannot convey. For instance, when people visit a museum included about war, they can see solder's uniform, understand about the process of their independent and emphazy their strugglers to thankfull for their's death in protect peaceful. Moreover, museums and galleries have vital cultural hubs, allowing people to symbolize the identity of a region. As a result, a magnet for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I firmly convinced that online experience in art is really useful; however, the direction experience in vital cultural hubs is more essential.

review.overall: Em theo đúng hướng bài: thừa nhận công nghệ giúp tiếp cận từ xa, rồi bảo vệ trải nghiệm tại bảo tàng và vai trò cộng đồng. Em nêu Louvre và bộ quân phục ở bảo tàng chiến tranh làm ví dụ. Tuy nhiên, mức kiểm soát câu và từ vựng còn yếu: 'in explore', 'still in needed', 'whom cannot afford', 'their's death in protect peaceful' và mảnh câu 'As a result, a magnet...' làm nhiều ý không truyền đạt được. Cụm 'a cup of tea with art' cũng dùng sai thành ngữ để nói người yêu nghệ thuật. Em cần nghiêm túc viết lại từng câu sai, đối chiếu mẫu buổi học và tự soát chủ ngữ–động từ trước khi nộp bản sửa.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that the development of technology can enable individuals to explore historical objects and works of art online; therefore, public museums and art galleries will be no longer needed. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, modern technology offers accessible ways to experience history and culture. Firstly, high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. This can be seen in the way Louvre Museum offers online exhibitions that people interested in art can explore from home, allowing them to admire artworks at little or no cost. Furthermore, people who cannot afford a museum visit or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I believe that public museums and art galleries are still needed for the unique experiences and cultural benefits they offer. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Viewing an artefact in person evokes emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For instance, when people visit a war museum, they can see a soldier's uniform and learn about the struggle for independence, which helps them appreciate the soldiers' sacrifices for peace. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. It naturally follows that they attract tourists and facilitate bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that online experience in art is useful; however, direct experience in museums and art galleries remains essential.

Overall, there was an increase in the amount of gas used in the UK while an opposite trend was observed in the case of oil and coal. Also of note is that gas consistently had the highest figures throughout the entire chart.

To elaborate, in 1990, an impressive 310 and 270 million tons of coal and oil respectively was used in the UK, with a subsequent fall to 250 and around 240 million tons. A growth, conversely, was seen in the figures of gas, from roughly 230 to 240 million tons at the same period time.

Regarding to the latter of timeline, the amount of coal and oil sources, which was used in the UK, witnessed the most pronounced fall, at approximately 190 and 210 million tons in 2010. paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows the amount of carbon emitted from oil, coal and gas in the UK between 1990 and 2010. The figures are measured in millions of tons at five-year intervals.

Overall, gas emissions increased throughout the period, whereas emissions from coal and oil declined from their starting levels. Coal produced the largest amount of emissions at the beginning, but gas overtook the other fuels by 2000 and remained the largest source until 2010.

In 1990, coal emissions stood at about 310 million tons, compared with approximately 270 million tons for oil and 220 million for gas. Coal's figure fell to around 280 million in 1995 and 250 million in 2000. Oil dropped to about 240 million tons in 1995 but recovered to roughly 260 million in 2000. By contrast, gas rose at each point during this first decade, reaching about 300 million tons in 2000.

From 2000 to 2010, the emissions from both coal and oil continued to fall. Coal declined from around 250 to 190 million tons, while oil decreased from roughly 260 to 210 million tons. Across the full period, coal recorded the larger net fall, of about 120 million tons, compared with oil's decrease of around 60 million. Gas followed the opposite trend in the last decade, rising from approximately 300 million tons in 2000 to a peak of about 320 million in 2010. It therefore finished as the highest of the three fuels.

You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

paragraphs: It is argued that one of the most essential subjects at school is history; however, some others say that subjects which is related to science and technology are more important in today's development. From my perspective, each subject in this argument have their own benefits in the development of world.

On the one hand, history is not only have its own benefits but also is one of the part to develop science and technology. Initially, history helps student understand exactly about themselves, the past of their family and the cultural of their country which can lead them to respect everything in the present. As a result, many motivations can creat to promote young generations develop themselves. Moreover, each history' lesson allow not only individuals but also scientists have valuable knowledge to not fail when create new inventions which helps the future.
review.overall: Em đã nêu cả hai quan điểm ở mở bài và thể hiện ý riêng rằng mỗi nhóm môn có lợi ích. Đoạn thân bài trình bày giá trị của lịch sử qua hiểu biết gia đình, văn hóa và bài học cho người làm khoa học; đây là hướng có thể phát triển. Tuy nhiên, bài dừng sau đoạn lịch sử, chưa có phần thực sự giải thích vì sao có người ưu tiên khoa học–công nghệ và cũng chưa kết lại lập trường. Em nên hoàn thiện phần còn thiếu trước, rồi sửa các câu dài có nhiều động từ không khớp như 'history is not only have' và 'each history’ lesson allow'.

paragraphs.text: Some people consider history one of the most valuable subjects at school, while others believe science and technology matter more today. In my view, both areas of study offer distinct benefits, and neither should be excluded from a student's education.

On the one hand, history helps students understand their families' past and the culture of their country. By learning how earlier generations lived and made decisions, young people may come to value the traditions they see around them. Historical study also encourages them to examine the results of past actions rather than accept simple stories without evidence. These habits can be useful beyond a history classroom. For example, researchers developing a new tool might learn how people dealt with a similar problem before and consider why an earlier attempt succeeded or failed. History therefore offers both cultural knowledge and a way to reflect on previous experience.

On the other hand, science and technology give students knowledge they can apply to current practical problems. Science lessons can teach them to test an explanation and check whether the evidence supports it, while technology classes may help them use digital tools effectively. A student who learns how to collect and compare information, for instance, can make a better decision when faced with a technical problem at work. These subjects are also relevant to many modern careers, which explains why some people give them greater priority than history. Their practical value does not erase the cultural value of studying the past.

In conclusion, history and science answer different educational needs. I would keep both in the school curriculum: history helps students understand people and earlier choices, while science and technology help them investigate and solve present-day problems.
